correctness.rationale: Every white side of cardinality >=3 is invariant under forcing because each opposite blue vertex misses at most one white neighbor; pairs of unmatched whites are likewise frozen. A separate completion lemma proves all cases with at most one white in a part, including the a=3 exception. With two whites on both sides the initial move exists precisely when matched index sets differ. Counting allowable white occupancy pairs gives five coefficients and exact number threshold. The standalone graph-simulation verifier exhausts 407040 subsets in 130 boards plus 60824 selected large-board subsets, but infinite correctness rests on proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural three-parameter perturbation of the classical K_{a,b} zero-forcing polynomial, a graph invariant introduced for counting initial controllability/propagation configurations. The full polynomial and all successful sets, including the perfect matching-deleted crown boundary, are determined by a sharp two-whites-per-part structural theorem. The phase transition Z=N-2,N-3,N-4 exposes why the first two matching deletions change propagation capacity and later deletions do not; positive-t coefficients are not implied by the known undeleted formula. Exact counts of minimum sets enable comparison of robustness of initial placements.
